The Costs for a DBS At Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT), roles that require a DBS check are subject to a cost recovery policy. This means that the cost of submitting and processing a DBS application if you are successful and join us, will be deducted from your salary within the first three months of employment. If, however, you withdraw from a conditional offer after the DBS process has begun, you will still be liable for the cost incurred. For more information about the cost of the various types of DBS, please visit: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dbs-fees-are-changing-in-december DBS Update Service Candidates are also expected to register with the DBS Update Service which must be completed within 30 days of the certificate being issued. This helps streamline future employment checks and supports safer recruitment practices. For more information, please visit the DBS Update Service.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for an Administrator to join our friendly and busy team at The Arch Medical Practice. This is an important role supporting the day-to-day running of the practice and helping us to deliver an efficient, high-quality service to our patients. The successful candidate will provide administrative support to the clinical and non-clinical teams, ensuring that patient information, correspondence and practice processes are managed accurately and efficiently. The role will involve a variety of administrative tasks, including handling incoming and outgoing correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records, processing information, supporting clinical workflows and responding to queries from colleagues and other healthcare professionals. You will play an important part in ensuring that the practice runs smoothly, supporting the wider team and helping to make sure that administrative processes are completed in a timely and organised manner. This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who is organised, reliable and has excellent attention to detail. You will need to be confident working in a busy environment, able to manage competing priorities and have good communication and IT skills. We are a large, supportive GP training practice caring for over 24,000 patients. We value our staff, encourage learning and development, and recognise the important contribution every member of the team makes to providing safe, effective and compassionate patient care. The role will involve providing administrative support across a range of practice functions, with particular responsibility for coordinating safeguarding administration. This will include maintaining safeguarding records, monitoring actions and ensuring relevant information is accurately recorded and followed up. The postholder will be responsible for managing patient recalls and monitoring outstanding actions to ensure patients are invited for appropriate reviews and follow-up. They will also support clinical and administrative audits, including gathering information, updating records and monitoring progress against agreed actions. Other duties will include clinical and administrative coding, maintaining accurate patient information, processing correspondence, preparing reports and supporting the practice with routine data management. The role will also involve providing administrative support for practice meetings, including preparing agendas, taking minutes, recording decisions and maintaining action logs to ensure agreed actions are followed through. The successful candidate will need to be highly organised, methodical and able to manage their own workload, ensuring that important deadlines, reviews and follow-up actions are not missed. Confidentiality, accuracy and good attention to detail are essential. Main Purpose of the Role To provide comprehensive administrative support to the practice, with specific responsibility for safeguarding administration, patient recalls, clinical and administrative audits and maintaining accurate patient records. The postholder will support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice, working closely with clinical and non-clinical colleagues to ensure that administrative processes are completed accurately, efficiently and within agreed timescales. Act as the practice Safeguarding Administration Lead, providing administrative support to the clinical safeguarding leads. Maintain and update safeguarding registers and records for adults and children. Ensure safeguarding information and relevant documentation are accurately recorded and appropriately filed within patient records. Monitor safeguarding correspondence, referrals and incoming information, ensuring these are brought to the attention of the appropriate clinician. Maintain safeguarding action logs and monitor outstanding administrative actions. Support the organisation of safeguarding meetings and multidisciplinary discussions. Ensure relevant safeguarding documentation is processed and shared appropriately, in accordance with practice procedures and information governance requirements. Escalate any safeguarding concerns or urgent correspondence promptly to the appropriate clinical lead. Provide administrative support for the practice recall system. Identify and contact patients requiring reviews, investigations, monitoring or follow-up. Monitor outstanding recalls and maintain accurate records of invitations and patient responses. Follow up patients who have not responded to invitations in accordance with practice protocols. Support the monitoring of patients requiring regular reviews for long-term conditions and other clinical requirements. Assist with DNA (Did Not Attend) management, identifying missed appointments and supporting appropriate follow-up. Maintain accurate recall information and report any outstanding issues to the relevant clinical team. Lead and undertake practice audits as directed by the Practice Manager and clinical leads. Identify patients and gather relevant information for audit purposes. Extract, collate and accurately record data from clinical systems. Prepare audit reports and present findings where required. Maintain audit records and action plans, monitoring progress against agreed actions. Support the practice with clinical governance activities and quality improvement initiatives. Assist with the collection of evidence for enhanced services, contractual requirements and CQC compliance. Input relevant information into patient healthcare records accurately and in a timely manner. Undertake clinical coding of incoming correspondence, documents and other information in accordance with practice protocols and training. Process hospital letters, clinical correspondence and other patient documentation, ensuring information is directed appropriately. Maintain accurate patient demographic and registration information. Process new patient registrations, changes to patient details and deductions from the practice list. Support the maintenance of accurate patient records and undertake data quality checks as required. Provide administrative support for practice and multidisciplinary team meetings. Prepare meeting agendas and relevant documentation. Attend meetings as required and produce accurate minutes. Maintain meeting action logs, recording agreed actions, responsible individuals and timescales. Monitor outstanding actions and follow up with relevant colleagues. Provide general administrative and secretarial support to the clinical and management teams as required. Deal with patients and visitors both face to face and over the telephone in a professional, friendly and helpful manner. Welcome patients and visitors to the practice and direct enquiries to the appropriate team or service. Support the administration of the practice total triage system. Handle routine enquiries and pass clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional. Provide reception cover during periods of staff absence or increased demand. Support the opening and closing of the practice in accordance with the duty rota. Act as a chaperone when required, following appropriate training and practice procedures. Support the delivery of enhanced services and other practice requirements. Contribute to the effective running of the wider multidisciplinary team. Participate in local initiatives and projects to improve service delivery and patient care. Attend community events and support activities to promote the practice. Participate in shared learning, training and development opportunities. Complete all mandatory training and induction programmes. Maintain confidentiality and comply with data protection, information governance and practice policies. Understand and comply with current safeguarding legislation and practice procedures relating to children and adults. Follow all practice policies, procedures and protocols, including health and safety requirements. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, as requested by the Practice Manager or partners.

title: Care Navigator Receptionist

As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a vital role in ensuring they receive the right support and are directed to the most appropriate healthcare professional or service. You will provide a professional and welcoming experience whether interacting with patients face to face, over the telephone or through digital channels. We are seeking someone with excellent communication skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to remain calm and compassionate when dealing with a wide range of patient needs. In return, you will become part of a dedicated team committed to providing high quality patient care, with opportunities for ongoing development and training. If you are motivated, reliable and passionate about making a difference within primary care, we would love to hear from you. The successful candidate will provide reception, care navigation and administrative support to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Duties include managing patient enquiries, coordinating appointments, processing prescriptions, handling correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records and supporting clinicians and colleagues with a variety of administrative tasks. You will communicate with patients through multiple channels, signpost them to appropriate services, process referrals and documentation, and ensure information is recorded accurately and confidentially. The role requires excellent organisational skills, confidence using computer systems and the ability to prioritise a varied workload while maintaining a high standard of customer service. You will also contribute to maintaining a safe, welcoming and efficient environment for patients and staff, working closely with the wider practice team to support the delivery of high-quality healthcare services. To provide a high-quality, professional reception and administrative service to patients, clinicians, colleagues and other healthcare professionals. Support care navigation by directing patients to the most appropriate clinician or service. Process urgent appointment requests and home visit requests in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate and up-to-date appointment systems. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone, email and other digital communication channels. Register new patients and temporary residents and explain practice procedures. Process payments for private services and issue receipts where required. Ensure patient samples are forwarded to the appropriate department or member of staff. Maintain tidy and welcoming reception and waiting areas. Ensure information leaflets and patient resources are replenished as required. Undertake opening and closing procedures and support the security of the premises. Maintain electronic and manual filing systems. Administrative Duties Work in accordance with practice policies, procedures and protocols. Process repeat prescription requests accurately and efficiently. Respond to patient enquiries received through the practice website. Process incoming electronic correspondence from hospitals and external organisations. Scan and accurately file patient correspondence within electronic records. Complete administrative tasks requested by clinicians and management. Type referral letters and process electronic referrals as required. Contact patients regarding appointments, test results and other healthcare-related matters. Support registration of new patients and updates to patient demographic information. Ensure all correspondence, reports and results are filed within the correct patient record. Use care navigation principles to direct patients to the most appropriate service. Provide a sensitive and supportive service in response to patients' needs. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Support clinicians and the wider practice team as required. Act as a chaperone when necessary and appropriately trained. Ensure clinical and administrative areas remain well stocked and organised. Assist in maintaining a safe, secure and clean working environment. Undertake other reasonable duties as requested by the Practice Manager or clinical team. The post holder will have access to confidential information relating to patients, carers, staff and the business of the practice. All information must be treated as strictly confidential and handled in accordance with practice policies, data protection legislation and professional standards. The post holder will be expected to maintain a good understanding of safeguarding responsibilities, identify concerns and follow appropriate procedures for raising and referring safeguarding issues relating to children and adults. The post holder will contribute to maintaining a safe working environment by complying with practice health and safety procedures, infection prevention and control guidance, and by reporting potential risks and hazards promptly. The post holder will support and promote equality, diversity and inclusion, treating patients, carers and colleagues with dignity, respect and fairness at all times. The post holder will work collaboratively with colleagues and external agencies, communicate effectively with patients and healthcare professionals, and contribute positively to the performance and development of the practice team.
